name: Diagonal Butterfly Spread (McMillan)
aliases: long-dated strangle financed by near-term sales
summary: A long-dated long strangle (or straddle) financed by repeatedly selling near-term strangles at strikes inside it - named in Options as a Strategic Investment, and the only structure in the bank whose economics come from a sequence of sales rather than one position.

legs.strike_rule: front month, call delta 0.15-0.25 - in the CLASSIC form this strike is INSIDE (below) the long call strike, which makes it uncovered
legs.dte_rule: front expiry, 21-45 DTE, resold each cycle

legs.strike_rule: front month, |put delta| 0.15-0.25, INSIDE (above) the long put strike in the classic form

max_profit: Unbounded in principle: the long strangle's convexity plus the accumulated front-month credits once the longs are paid for
max_loss: In the CLASSIC (inside-strike) form: UNDEFINED, because the short call sits below the long call and the short put above the long put. In the level-3 form: the net debit paid, less all credits collected.
breakevens: Moves every cycle; recompute after each front-month sale as long strangle cost minus cumulative credits, spread around the current spot

greeks.delta: near zero if the strangles are centered
greeks.gamma: negative in the front, positive in the back
greeks.theta: positive while the front shorts are alive

typical_dte: back 180-365 DTE, front 21-45 DTE resold 6-12 times
when_to_use: INCLUDED FOR COMPLETENESS - the classic form is NOT TRADEABLE AT LEVEL 3. Used when long-dated IV is cheap relative to front-month IV (steep contango in the term structure) and the goal is to own a free long strangle by expiry.
entry_rules: BLOCKED in its classic form: front shorts struck inside the long strikes are uncovered on both sides; requires Alpaca options level 4.

LEVEL 3 FORM (permitted, and the only version this system may run): buy the back-month leg as an ATM straddle (or a strangle with strikes INSIDE the shorts), and sell the front-month strangle OUTSIDE those strikes. Every short call then has a long call at an equal or lower strike, and every short put a long put at an equal or higher strike, so both shorts are option-covered and the structure is a double diagonal with a long-vol tilt.
Term-structure gate: back-month IV <= front-month IV minus 2 vol points at entry.
Back-month debit <= 4% of equity; the whole structure is a multi-month capital commitment.
Front-month credit per cycle >= 1/8 of the back-month debit, otherwise the financing plan does not finish inside a year.
All four strikes OI >= 250; no single names with earnings in the front cycle.
management_rules: Resell the front strangle on the day after each front expiry or on the 21-DTE roll, whichever comes first, always at delta 0.15-0.25 and always outside the long strikes.
Track cumulative credits against the back-month debit; once credits >= debit, the long strangle is free and the system may stop selling and simply hold convexity.
If the underlying moves more than 1 long-strike width, re-center by rolling the untested front short in, never by moving a long strike out.
Stop selling front strangles entirely when front-month IV rank falls below 20 - there is nothing left to harvest and the shorts only cap the convexity.
Abandon the program (close everything) if cumulative credits are below 40% of the debit with less than 90 DTE left on the back month.
exit_rules: ASSIGNMENT GUARD: both front legs are short; flatten both by 15:30 ET on every front expiration day, without exception.
Close any front short at extrinsic < $0.10 or |delta| >= 0.85; close short calls before any ex-dividend date while ITM.
Never let a front short expire ITM on the theory that the back-month long covers it - the long is an option, not shares, and assignment still delivers stock overnight.
Close the back-month legs rather than exercising them.
Hard stop: if a front short is assigned despite the guards, close the resulting share position at the next open and halt the program for review.
assignment_risk: Two short legs alive at all times, refreshed every cycle, which multiplies the number of assignment windows by the number of cycles. In the level-3 form each short is covered by a longer-dated long of the same right, so an assignment is recoverable by exercising that long - but it is still shares delivered into an account that must never be assigned.
buying_power: Level-3 form: the diagonal spread requirement per side (strike difference x 100 where the short is further OTM, otherwise the net debit). Classic form: naked margin on both front legs.
liquidity_needs: A chain with genuine LEAPS liquidity and weekly or monthly front cycles - SPY, QQQ, IWM and a handful of mega-caps only.
common_mistakes: Running the classic inside-strike version without level 4 and discovering the naked exposure at the first test; counting credits collected as profit before the back-month debit is recovered; rolling a long strike out to 'fix' a tested side, which converts the trade into a naked ratio.
zero_dte_notes: Not applicable; the front cycle should never be shorter than 21 DTE in this structure.
family: Completeness gap-fill (cross-family): ratio/naked-financed put and call structures, quantity-unbalanced condors and strangles, stock+option overlays and monetizations, capital-protection and hybrid builds, 0DTE four-leg income, volatility-surface and relative-value trades, event-driven overlays, and roll/adjustment structures
blocked_because: needs Alpaca options level 4; this account is level 3. Alpaca rejects it with 'account not eligible to trade uncovered option contracts'. Raising the level is an Alpaca approval, not a code change.
